questions.question: When drivers turn, they usually:

options.text: Look in the direction of the turn.
Look in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, drivers usually look in the direction they are turning. Even if a driver does not signal, their body movements can show they plan to turn.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stand as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: Stand as far away from the fire as possible when using a fire extinguisher. Aim at the base of the fire, not at the flames. If you are unsure which extinguisher to use, wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, do all of the following except:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: When checking your windshield, look for cracks or damage that could block your view. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and loose attachment.

questions.question: One way to prevent drowsiness while driving is to:

options.text: Get a full night of sleep before the trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a full night of sleep before the trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is very dangerous. To prevent drowsiness, get a full night of sleep before your trip, travel with a passenger, drive during hours when you are normally awake, and avoid medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise increases your energy and helps you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers speeding
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully and slowly near workers.

questions.question: Front tire tread depth should be at least ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on front tires. Other tires need a tread depth of 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: If being tailgated, you should:

options.text: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the space between your vehicle and the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead. This reduces the need for sudden speed or direction changes and makes it easier for the tailgater to pass.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, you should:

options.text: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop an engine fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless necessary.

questions.question: The "crack-the-whip" effect can:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn over a trailer.
questions.explanation: Trailers can overturn because of the "crack-the-whip" effect. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip. Drivers should understand how this effect works on their vehicle and drive safely.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a sign of tire failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Smoother steering
questions.explanation: Signs of tire failure include a loud "bang" sound from a blowout or heavy thumping and vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear of your vehicle fishtails, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: You must act quickly when brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle moves. This makes it harder to stop.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a sign that a driver is getting tired?
questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of tired driving include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, missing exits or traffic signs, drifting from your lane, and feeling restless or irritable. Feeling hungry is not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: When does hydroplaning usually happen?

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on surfaces where water has collected. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Under-inflated tires and worn tread make hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill and there is no escape ramp, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Drive into an open field.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp first. If no ramp is available, find another place to stop your vehicle, such as an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections are:

options.text: Needed only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required by law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip, no matter how long or short the trip is.

questions.question: Baffled tanks:

options.text: Should be inspected by an electrician.
Allow liquid cargo to flow through the tank.
Control the temperature of the liquid cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow liquid cargo to flow through the tank.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have bulkheads with holes inside them. These bulkheads reduce front-to-back surge while still letting liquid flow through the whole tank.

questions.question: A high center of gravity in a tank means:

options.text: It gets very good gas mileage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can roll over easily.
questions.explanation: Tanks have high centers of gravity. This makes tank vehicles more likely to roll over than other vehicles, especially when driven at high speeds in turns and curves.

questions.question: When a tank stops, the liquid inside may surge. This can:

options.text: Cause the truck to stop too quickly.
Cause the truck to be pushed forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause the truck to be pushed forward.
questions.explanation: When liquid surges in a partially filled tank, the truck gets pushed in the direction of the wave. On a slippery surface, the surge may push the truck forward into an intersection or another vehicle.

questions.question: A loaded trailer with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Gets better gas mileage than an empty trailer.
Is usually more stable than an empty trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can roll over easily.
questions.explanation: A trailer with a high center of gravity is at greater risk of rolling over than a trailer with a low center of gravity.

questions.question: The service air line is often controlled by the foot brake and is attached to the ____ valves.
questions.correctAnswerText: Relay
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air and is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which allow the trailer brakes to be applied quickly.
